title: Check the web address

cards.text: Read the web address before you log in or pay. CISA says fake sites can use addresses with small spelling changes or a wrong ending, like .com instead of .gov.
cards.line: Read the sign before you enter.

cards.text: The FTC says https means the connection is encrypted, but it does not prove the site is honest. Check the address too.
cards.line: Https protects the trip, not the truth.

cards.text: Type a company address yourself. The FTC says to type the website address directly into your browser if you know it. That helps you reach the right site.
cards.line: Use a path you already know.

options: A site that is always honest

takeaway: Check the address, even when you see https.

sources.name: CISA, tips to stay safe while surfing the web, part 2

situations.text: Does https alone prove that a site is honest?
situations.why: It means the connection is encrypted, but it does not prove the site is honest.

situations.text: Before you pay on a site, you read its web address for small spelling changes or a wrong ending.
situations.why: CISA says fake sites can use addresses with small spelling changes.
